title: Commencement Terms for a New Office Pantry & Beverage Program Agreement
content:
A pantry programme is drawn up as a proposal against the tier whose entry gate the site meets on headcount, plumbed water, storage space and annual spend, and it starts with the first standing delivery. The clauses below govern how an Office Pantry & Beverage Program agreement is opened and brought into service.

**Clause 1 — tier written.** The programme is written against the tier whose entry gate the site meets on all four measures. Where the site does not meet the entry gate of the tier asked for, the programme is written at the highest tier whose entry gate the site does meet.

**Clause 2 — state of the programme.** A programme is only opened or started while it stands proposed or already active, and a proposal withdrawn before signature closes without charge. The status standing on the programme is read before the programme is opened or started, from Larkspur Table's own record of that programme rather than from what the client reports.

**Clause 3 — charges raised at commencement.** The fitting charge and the refundable equipment deposit printed against the tier are invoiced when the programme starts, and a proposal withdrawn before signature carries neither.

**Clause 4 — fitting lead time and the first delivery.** Fitting takes the lead days printed against the tier, counted in calendar days from signature, and the first delivery is scheduled on the standing delivery weekday on or after that lead time.

**Clause 5 — the standing list at the start.** The standing list is set at the start from the product count printed against the tier, and changes to it need the order lead days printed against the same tier.

## Reading clause 4 at its boundary

The lead time runs in calendar days from signature, and the first standing delivery takes the standing delivery weekday on or after it. Where the lead time ends on the standing delivery weekday itself, that day is the first standing delivery. Where it ends on the day after that weekday, the first standing delivery is the next occurrence of the standing weekday.

## Points of judgement

Question: the client asks for a tier whose entry gate their site does not meet on storage space, although it meets the headcount and annual spend figures.
Answer: the programme is written at the highest tier whose entry gate the site does meet on headcount, plumbed water, storage space and annual spend together.

Question: a proposal is withdrawn before signature.
Answer: it closes without charge; neither the fitting charge nor the refundable equipment deposit printed against the tier is invoiced, because those two fall due when the programme starts.

Question: the programme already stands closed.
Answer: closed is not one of the two statuses that admit an opening or a start; only a programme standing proposed or already active is opened or started.
